report_fields.summary:
WRI responds to the UNEP overshoot finding, arguing return below 1.5 °C remains technically feasible via clean
energy, carbon removal at scale and adaptation, and citing evidence that every US$1 invested in adaptation
yields more than US$10 in benefits. The 10:1 adaptation benefit-cost ratio is a headline figure for protection-gap
and resilience-investment arguments.

verified_information.summary: WASHINGTON (September 2, 2026) — UNEP today published Limiting Overshoot, its first report on the likelihood and consequences of exceeding 1.5°C of global warming. It finds that global temperature rise is set to cross 1.5°C, likely within the next few years, pushing climate risks to increasingly dangerous levels. The report also finds that temperatures can still be brought back down in line with the long-term goals of the Paris Agreement.

appearances.summary: ILO reports rising temperatures linked to higher worker mortality in Colombia — concrete evidence for health and life actuaries calibrating heat-mortality assumptions under climate scenarios and occupational-exposure models.
appearances.title: High temperatures linked to increased mortality among workers in Colombia

enrichment.summary: ILO reports rising temperatures linked to higher worker mortality in Colombia — concrete evidence for health and life actuaries calibrating heat-mortality assumptions under climate scenarios and occupational-exposure models.

pdf_occurrences.anchor_text: ilo.org — heat and worker mortality in Colombia

report_fields.source_label: ilo.org — heat and worker mortality in Colombia
report_fields.summary:
Above 32 °C, excess mortality reaches 0.09 deaths per 1,000 workers overall, rising to 1.33 for assemblers, 0.40 for
health associate professionals, 0.26 for agricultural workers and 0.21 for teaching professionals; between 26 and 32 °C
the excess is 0.04 per 1,000. These are directly applicable occupational heat-mortality loadings for life, disability and
workers' compensation pricing, and the finding that only 53% of Colombia's workforce held occupational-risk cover in
December 2024 quantifies the associated protection gap.

appearances.summary: WMO describes how an upstream ice-and-rock avalanche and possible temporary river blockage may have contributed to Nepal's flash floods; the trigger was still under investigation. Rapid downstream water-level rises and damaged monitoring stations illustrate cascading, cross-border hazards and the need for stronger observations, data exchange and actionable early warnings.
appearances.title: Flood Tragedy Nepal Highlights Cross Border and Cascading Risks

enrichment.summary: WMO describes how an upstream ice-and-rock avalanche and possible temporary river blockage may have contributed to Nepal's flash floods; the trigger was still under investigation. Rapid downstream water-level rises and damaged monitoring stations illustrate cascading, cross-border hazards and the need for stronger observations, data exchange and actionable early warnings.

pdf_occurrences.anchor_text: Flood tragedy in Nepal highlights cross-border and cascading risks

report_fields.summary:
An ice-and-rock avalanche on the Tibet border triggered a flash flood on 26 August; 359 deaths were confirmed
by 27 August with around 10,000 households affected, and the Trishuli River rose nine metres in thirty minutes.
A textbook cascading, cross-border cryosphere hazard that sits poorly in conventional flood catastrophe models,
and material for Himalayan hydropower and infrastructure exposures.

verified_information.summary: “WMO sends condolences to the victims of the terrible disaster and expresses its solidarity with the communities affected by this devastating flood,” said WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo. "The Rasuwa flood highlights the growing challenge posed by cascading hazards in high-mountain regions, where changes and instabilities in the cryosphere can rapidly translate into destructive downstream impacts across national borders. The event underscores why we need to close gaps across the warning value chain - from sustained monitoring and timely detection of emerging hazards, to resilient observing

appearances.summary: The article explains that Paris-consistent modeled pathways require carbon dioxide removal of 2.7–4.1 billion metric tons annually by 2035 and 6.5–13.3 billion by 2050, alongside steep emissions reductions, to support net zero and eventual temperature decline after overshoot. It also examines government policies, certification frameworks, monitoring and reporting protocols, and safeguards intended to scale carbon removal while addressing permanence and environmental risks.
appearances.title: As the US Carbon Dioxide Removal Market Retreats, Other Governments Step Up

enrichment.summary: The article explains that Paris-consistent modeled pathways require carbon dioxide removal of 2.7–4.1 billion metric tons annually by 2035 and 6.5–13.3 billion by 2050, alongside steep emissions reductions, to support net zero and eventual temperature decline after overshoot. report_fields.summary:
US federal CDR support has been withdrawn — the DOE Purchase Pilot Prize delayed and direct air capture
hubs halted — while the EU, Canada, Germany and the UK advance beyond voluntary markets, against a need
to remove 2.7–4.1 Gt CO2 per year by 2035. Policy-divergence risk of this kind is a concrete transition-risk driver
and complicates any single global CDR assumption in scenario work.

verified_information.summary: As the United States pulls back, momentum for carbon dioxide removal is building elsewhere, propelled by government policies and frameworks that extend beyond voluntary markets. By: Dan Lashof, Danielle Riedl and Clea Schumer September 10, 2026 Explore More: carbon removalcarbon capture and storage (CCS) Two workers stand near Climeworks' Mammoth carbon dioxide collector container tower in Iceland. occurrences.anchor_text: Asking Better Questions on Nature: For Bank Chief Risk Officers and Risk Committees

report_fields.summary:
A TNFD guide produced with UNEP FI, structured around ten questions for bank chief risk officers and risk
committees to test exposure to nature-related financial risk across credit and investment portfolios, with the
headline quantification that pollinator decline alone puts up to USD 577 billion of annual global crop production at
risk. It positions nature loss as a systemic financial-stability issue to be handled inside mainstream risk
frameworks rather than as a disclosure exercise, and is the bank-CRO companion to TNFD's earlier CFO and
asset-owner editions. Relevant to actuaries working on nature-related financial risk and on agricultural credit and
crop exposures.
Caveat. Partial verification. The UNEP FI landing page carries “September 2026” only and there is no matching item in
the UNEP FI news listing. Third-party coverage (Sustainable Japan, 18 September 2026) corroborates a release around
17–18 September but also states only the month. Title, URL, content and month are confirmed; the day is approximate.

occurrences.anchor_text: CatIQ raises Montreal West Island flooding insured loss estimate to C$442m

report_fields.summary:
CatIQ's third estimate for the 20–21 June 2026 Montreal West Island thunderstorm flooding rises to CAD 442
million, from CAD 411 million in August and CAD 409 million initially — a 7.5% increase since August and
continued upward development. CatIQ notes pluvial flash flooding was the story of the summer for Canadian
catastrophes, with six major events between June and August across Ontario and Quebec generating over
30,000 personal property claims. Pluvial flood development patterns of this kind bear directly on IBNR
assumptions for urban flood.

occurrences.anchor_text: WMO update, 21 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Three deliverables assessing the observational base underpinning climate services. In-situ networks supporting
the 55 Essential Climate Variables still depend heavily on short-term research projects, in-kind contributions or
volunteers, with material gaps across Africa, South America, Southeast Asia and the polar regions; satellite
observation covers 42 of the 55 ECVs, and a February 2026 survey of 33 climate experts found communication
with decision-makers, not data access or quality, the most-cited barrier to uptake. This is the observational-input
risk sitting underneath every catastrophe model and physical-risk scorecard — known geographic gaps and
funding fragility in the underlying networks are a source of parameter uncertainty that is rarely priced.

occurrences.anchor_text: FAO newsroom, 23 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Joint statement of Somalia's Federal Government and UN agencies projecting 5.4 million people in crisis-level
hunger or worse over October–December 2026, 1.5 million of them in emergency conditions, with El Niño-driven
Deyr-season flooding projected to expose 2.5–3.5 million people and displace around one million. A quantified,
country-scale El Niño impact projection of the kind directly usable for humanitarian and sovereign disaster-risk-
financing trigger design, and a live test of anticipatory-action payout timing.

occurrences.anchor_text: Gallagher Securities working on cat bond that will introduce new peril to the market

report_fields.summary:
Gallagher Securities' chief executive says the firm is structuring a transaction for a peril that has never been
securitised before, without naming it, and notes double-digit new sponsors come to market each year. Thin on
specifics, but carried as a watch item: a genuinely new peril class in the cat bond market would set modelling
and reserving precedent.
Caveat. The peril is not disclosed in the source and no issuance figures are given.

report_fields.summary:

occurrences.anchor_text: STATEMENT: UN Secretary-General's Climate Summit Calls for Faster, Fairer Climate Action

report_fields.summary:
WRI's response to the UNSG Climate Summit, organised around keeping 1.5°C within reach, mobilising finance
for developing countries, and — new emphasis — advancing adaptation during climate overshoot. Germany
announced a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap to 2045; WRI cites a benefit-cost ratio of more than 10:1
over a decade for adaptation spending. The formal arrival of “adaptation under overshoot” in the multilateral
agenda is the signal for scenario designers: it legitimises planning around temporary exceedance of 1.5°C rather
than treating it as a tail case.

report_fields.summary:
Estimates 775,000 jobs from nature tourism and agribusiness in Colombia by 2035 against a government-
identified pipeline of more than USD 32 billion in green investment opportunities. The transition-risk figure of note
is that about 4.7 million workers, roughly 22.6% of the current workforce, will be directly affected by the climate
transition, in a labour market where around 55% of workers were informally employed as of June 2026. A
concrete just-transition exposure quantification for an emerging-market sovereign, relevant both to sovereign
transition-risk scenarios and to life and health portfolios exposed to informal-sector displacement.

occurrences.anchor_text: BMA to prioritise substance of parametric risk transfer over contractual form for new PSPI

report_fields.summary:
The Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter responding to feedback on its January 2026
consultation for a dedicated Parametric Special Purpose Insurer class supporting structured, fully collateralised
parametric risk transfer. The BMA will look to the substance of risk transfer rather than contractual form,
admitting contracts structured as reinsurance, derivatives or swaps provided statutory requirements are met;
existing SPIs may transition, and some may write both indemnity and parametric business case by case. An
amendment to the Insurance Act 1978 is being drafted for Q4 2026. The most consequential regulatory
development of the window for parametric and index-based climate covers.

verified_primary_display.title: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

occurrences.anchor_text: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

report_fields.summary:
Documents a structural mismatch between policy incentive and buyer behaviour in the US voluntary market:
despite Section 45Q paying USD 180/t for direct air capture, DAC is only 2% of the largest US buyer's portfolio,
while biomass carbon removal and storage accounted for 96% of durable CDR purchase volume in 2025
(BECCS alone 69%). California's compliance programme has issued over 267 million offset credits through
2024, 81% from forest projects. The US CDR buyer base has doubled since 2022 to 69 buyers but average
purchase size has fallen — a thinning, not deepening, market.

report_fields.summary:
CCRIF SPC's parametric risk pool has grown to USD 1.8 billion of coverage limits for the current policy year, up
14.5% on June 2026 and 25% on the prior year. Membership stands at 39, with four new members this season
— Jamaica Public Service Company, National Water Commission Jamaica, Nevis Electricity Company and
Nevis Water Department — all utilities, evidencing extension beyond sovereigns into water and electric utilities.
Since 2007 CCRIF has made 82 payouts totalling USD 483 million, disbursed within 14 days of a qualifying
event. The clearest sovereign-risk-pool datapoint of the window and a working example of parametric basis-risk
design at scale.

occurrences.anchor_text: FAO newsroom, 22 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Third in an FAO series on the livestock sector's contribution to food security and sustainable agrifood systems.
Livestock supplies a third of global protein and roughly 40% of agricultural GDP (about USD 1.8 trillion) while
contributing 12% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, cattle the largest share and enteric methane a
major source; emission profiles differ by system, with low-external-input systems emitting less per unit area and
high-input systems less per kilogram of output. Relevant to transition risk in agricultural lending and insurance
books, and a counterweight to blanket sectoral exclusion approaches.

occurrences.anchor_text: Savings, loans and resilience: it takes a village

report_fields.summary:
Village savings and loan associations in Côte d'Ivoire under the SAGA 2 project, where women farmers borrow
to fund mulching, composting and crop diversification against shifted rainfall seasons. Included at the margin as
evidence of informal, community-level adaptation finance filling the segment that sits beneath the practical reach
of microinsurance and parametric products.
Caveat. Qualitative only; the item carries no financial figures and is not formal disaster risk financing.

occurrences.anchor_text: What is the AO500? AlliedOffsets' carbon price index, explained

report_fields.summary:
Methodology note on the AO500, a retirement-weighted average price across the 500 highest-retirement-volume
carbon projects, built from over 17,000 price inputs a year and refreshed three times weekly; it closed at USD
6.30/t on 18 September 2026 against a 2026 range of USD 3.16–7.07 and a 2026 average to date of USD 6.04
(2024: USD 3.79). The companion Tradable20 index has averaged USD 2.58 below the AO500 in 2026. For
actuaries the AO500/Tradable20 spread is a direct, published measure of liquidity-tier basis risk in carbon-credit
valuation.

IN WINDOW 21 SEP 2026 DATA CARBON MARKETS
Methodology note on the AO500, a retirement-weighted average price across the 500 highest-retirement-volume
carbon projects, built from over 17,000 price inputs a year and refreshed three times weekly; it closed at USD
6.30/t on 18 September 2026 against a 2026 range of USD 3.16–7.07 and a 2026 average to date of USD 6.04
(2024: USD 3.79). The companion Tradable20 index has averaged USD 2.58 below the AO500 in 2026. For
actuaries the AO500/Tradable20 spread is a direct, published measure of liquidity-tier basis risk in carbon-credit
valuation.

occurrences.anchor_text: Property reinsurance prices most likely to fall 7.5% to 15% in 2027: Moody's survey

report_fields.summary:
Moody's survey of reinsurance buyers points to property reinsurance prices falling 7.5–15% in 2027 following
double-digit reductions in 2026, with 86% expecting declines, up from 74% who expected declines for 2026 —
buyers having under-called the severity of the 2026 softening. A meaningful minority expect falls beyond 15%,
and 28% plan to increase their use of alternative capital in 2027. Relevant to anyone setting 2027 reinsurance
cost assumptions or modelling the cost of buying additional climate-driven catastrophe capacity.

occurrences.anchor_text: 60% expect property cat rates to fall, 86% expect T&Cs to loosen: Fitch reinsurance survey

report_fields.summary:
Fitch finds 60% expect property catastrophe pricing to decline in 2027, a fifth of those by more than 10%, and
86% expect terms and conditions to loosen (58% selectively, 28% broadly). Fewer than 10% rank property or
property cat as a capital-allocation priority. Fitch's read is that persistent excess P&C capital will push
competition into terms-and-conditions erosion rather than headline rate — the more dangerous form of softening,
because loosened attachment points and hours clauses are not visible in rate indices.

report_fields.summary:
Technical brief framing climate risk assessment for electricity transmission and distribution networks and
integrating resilience measures across the project cycle, covering extreme heat, flooding, wildfire, landslide, and
sand and dust storms against network reliability, asset life and financial viability, with evidence from the
Mauritania–Mali Interconnection, Eastern Ethiopia Grid Reinforcement and Mozambique's Songo-Matambo. The
claimed cost–benefit evidence for adaptation spend is precisely the evidence base most often missing when
pricing resilience investment.
Caveat. Headline figures sit in the downloadable PDF; the landing page carries abstract-level text only.

occurrences.anchor_text: Swiss Re highlights growing catastrophe protection gap as nat cat losses rise 5-7% annually

report_fields.summary:
Swiss Re puts structural trend growth in insured nat-cat losses at 5–7% a year, with European wildfire losses
compounding an estimated 8–11% annually over recent decades. Modelled insured losses could reach roughly
USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak-loss scenario, and a 2017-style hurricane cluster alone pushes annual insured
losses above USD 120 billion, against 2025 global insured nat-cat losses of USD 120 billion. The 5–7% trend
rate is the single most citable figure this fortnight for calibrating loss-trend assumptions in catastrophe pricing
and ORSA scenarios.

occurrences.anchor_text: WMO bulletin shows successes and challenges in ozone layer recovery

report_fields.summary:
The annual ozone bulletin reports the 2025 Antarctic ozone hole as the fourth-to-fifth smallest since severe
depletion was first observed in 1992, with full recovery expected within several decades, and records UV
radiation rising by as much as 20% in parts of Europe since the mid-1990s, driven mainly by reduced cloud
cover. Marginal but retained on two counts: the Kigali Amendment HFC phase-down is a live transition-risk
exposure for the cooling and refrigeration value chain, and the UV trend is a slow-burn morbidity signal for life
and health portfolios.

occurrences.anchor_text: WMO news, 17 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Launch of the State of Global Water Resources 2025. 2025 was among the driest years for river discharge in
over 35 years, with below-normal flows across 36% of global basin area; for the seventh consecutive year basins
in normal condition were a minority at 34–38% against a 1991–2020 norm of 46%. Glaciers lost mass for a
fourth straight year across all regions, 1,400 gigatonnes over 2023–2025, and nearly two-thirds of monitored
groundwater wells sat outside historical norms. Asia and Africa accounted for at least 50% of water-related
extreme events and over 80% of associated deaths in the last five years. The headline finding — that the cycle
now oscillates between too little and too much rather than trending in one direction — directly degrades
stationarity assumptions in flood and drought models.
report_fields.title: WMO: Recent water trends have serious future implications

occurrences.anchor_text: NZAOA calls on private market asset managers to turn climate ambition into everyday practice

report_fields.summary:
The 85-member Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance published an updated Call to Action to Private Market Asset
Managers setting seven expectations of general partners across private equity, private debt, infrastructure and
real estate, including firm-level net-zero alignment, better financed-emissions data quality, engagement-led
decarbonisation and explicit integration of physical climate risk analysis, anchored on a principle of acting on
data available today rather than waiting for perfect data. Material for life and pension actuaries: private markets
are the segment where climate data is weakest and valuations least mark-to-market, and asset owners are now
setting explicit physical-risk expectations on general partners.

occurrences.anchor_text: Boosting action on climate and nature in focus

report_fields.summary:
Inger Andersen's address to the 175th meeting of the Committee of Permanent Representatives in Nairobi. Two
quantified claims are worth carrying into scenario work as sensitivities around central warming pathways: full
implementation of the Kigali Amendment could avoid up to 0.5°C of warming by end-century, and deploying
available methane abatement across fossil fuel, agriculture and waste could avoid up to 0.2°C by 2050. These
are the figures UNEP will repeat into COP31.

occurrences.anchor_text: New roadmap signals Africa's pathway for sustainable and resilient agriculture

report_fields.summary:
Marking ten years of the Initiative for the Adaptation of African Agriculture, FAO released The State of African
Agricultural Adaptation, 2016–2026: Assessment and Roadmap to 2036. Forty-six of 53 African countries have
costed combined adaptation needs of USD 566 billion across national plans — about USD 56 billion a year — of
which at least USD 80 billion is specifically agricultural, and that is a floor because 22 countries have not
itemised agriculture separately. This is the most usable denominator published this fortnight for African
adaptation protection-gap and sovereign-risk work.

occurrences.anchor_text: Busy August pushes Allstate's current aggregate year pre-tax cat losses to $3.15bn

report_fields.summary:
Allstate reported USD 748 million of pre-tax catastrophe losses in August 2026 from 21 separate events, half
from a single wind and hail occurrence, taking April–August aggregate pre-tax cat losses to USD 3.15 billion. Its
only current annual aggregate protection is the USD 150 million Class B tranche of Sanders Re III (Series 2023-
1), attaching at USD 4.78 billion with a USD 50 million per-event deductible, while a new USD 1 billion aggregate
excess-of-loss layer for 2026 attaches at USD 8.5 billion with a USD 1 million event deductible. A clean worked
illustration of how per-event deductibles inside aggregate structures create qualifying-loss uncertainty — a live
reserving and disclosure problem.

occurrences.anchor_text: As cat bond loss multiples tighten, AM Best urges investors towards greater selectivity

report_fields.summary:
AM Best reports cat bond loss multiples compressing to 2.5x in H1 2026 from 3.28x in H1 2025, with 2026 year-
to-date at 2.4x against 3.0x in 2025 and 3.71x in 2024. Weighted average spread fell 96 basis points while
expected loss on new issuance rose 30 basis points against H1 2025 — investors are being paid less for more
risk. Returns at 30 June 2026: Swiss Re Global Cat Bond Index 4.1%, ILS Advisers Index 3.9%. The
simultaneous fall in multiple and rise in expected loss is the sharpest risk-adjusted-return warning of the window
and bears directly on the cost and reliability of alternative capacity into the January 2027 renewals.

report_fields.summary:
Announcement of a joint ITU–WMO symposium on 28–30 September reviewing threats to the radio frequencies
underpinning weather forecasting, climate monitoring, water management and hazard early warning as demand
for wireless and satellite services accelerates. A non-obvious systemic dependency: degradation of protected
spectrum would directly reduce forecast skill and early-warning lead time, with knock-on effects for parametric
trigger reliability and catastrophe model input quality.

occurrences.anchor_text: Pacific ministers chart course for stronger weather and climate services

report_fields.summary:
The Fourth Pacific Meteorological Ministers Meeting in Nuku'alofa adopted the Siu-í-Álaimoana-Ki-Likutapu
Declaration committing to stronger National Meteorological and Hydrological Services and expanded multi-
hazard early warning, and advanced a Pacific Islands Meteorological Strategy 2027–2036. Tonga's Prime
Minister put the region's average annual cost of weather and climate events at half a billion US dollars, and the
meeting flagged El Niño conditions expected to peak between November 2026 and January 2027. Directly
relevant to Pacific disaster-risk-financing and parametric programme design, and to the early-warning cost–
benefit case underpinning resilience-linked pricing.

occurrences.anchor_text: How climate action can reduce security risks in the Hindu Kush Himalaya

report_fields.summary:
The Hindu Kush Himalaya supplies water to over 240 million people in the region and nearly two billion
downstream across 16 countries. Glacial ice was lost 65% faster in the 2010s than in the previous decade, with
projected 80% volume loss by 2100 on current emissions; the 2022 South Asian heatwave affected over one
billion people and the 2022 Pakistan floods hit 33 million people with over USD 30 billion in damage. Relevant to
compound physical-risk and correlated-loss assessment — glacial lake outburst flood, riverine flood and heat —
across a transboundary exposure base with very thin insurance penetration.

occurrences.anchor_text: Artemis, 22–23 September 2026 (updated)

report_fields.summary:
Hurricane Polo's intensification put the USD 175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric cat bond in
focus. The bond triggers on central pressure and location, requiring central pressure at or below 937 mb, with
payouts of 25% to 100% of principal by intensity and landfall location. Polo reached Category 5 with central
pressure as low as 892 mb while offshore, then weakened to 120 mph and 954 mb approaching Baja landfall,
making a trigger unlikely. A textbook illustration of parametric basis risk: peak intensity far inside the trigger
threshold, but in the wrong place at the wrong time.

urban resilience to flood and erosion hazards alongside infrastructure access, capacity building and emergency
response. Gully erosion is a material and poorly modelled loss driver in rapidly urbanising African cities, and this
is one of the few structured treatments of it in the adaptation literature.
Caveat. No numerical risk metrics on the landing page.

occurrences.anchor_text: COP31 Global Sustainable Insurance Summit to catalyze climate resilience across the economy

report_fields.summary:
UNEP and the Insurance Association of Türkiye will co-host the summit on 13–14 November 2026 at the
Insurance House, Antalya, during COP31, under the theme “The Climate Resilience Imperative”. The named
deliverable is the global launch of the PSI white paper From Vulnerability to Insurability: building resilient
communities and economies in an era of rising physical climate risk, with an agenda spanning insurability
valuation, resilient cities, MSME protection gaps, climate–nature linkages, climate-related health risk in
insurance, data gaps and low-carbon investment. This is the most directly actuarial scheduled publication on the
forward calendar and should be diarised for November.

headquarters, including climate-resilient cities, resilient health systems, food security, oceans, and a “Climate
Implementation Bridge”, and stated that strengthening observation, forecasting and early warning capacity is part
of the COP31 implementation approach. The presidency's emphasis on measurable implementation over
pledges, and on resilient cities and health systems, indicates where insurance-relevant COP31 outcomes are
most likely to land.

occurrences.anchor_text: Cool Leaders, a roadmap and nature for cooling: Global Cooling Pledge acts on heat

report_fields.summary:
At the Global Cooling Pledge Assembly in Singapore UNEP launched a Global Roadmap on Heat Resilience
covering schools, hospitals and energy systems, a Manufacturing Platform for efficient low-GWP equipment, and
the inaugural Cool Leaders awards; Brazil, Cambodia and Côte d'Ivoire launched a Nature for Cooling Challenge
backed by a USD 3 million GEF grant plus USD 33 million co-financing, targeting nature-based cooling that can
cut peak summer temperatures by up to 5°C. Global air-conditioner demand is projected to reach 5.6 billion units
by 2050, nearly triple today's level. Direct read-across to heat mortality and morbidity assumptions in life and
health portfolios, to heat-driven business interruption, and to the electricity-demand and HFC transition
exposures in the cooling value chain.

report_fields.summary:
CatIQ tallies over CAD 1.8 billion of insured losses from ten extreme weather events across Alberta,
Saskatchewan and Manitoba in summer 2026, the 9–10 June Saskatchewan/Manitoba severe storms alone at
CAD 900 million. Notably, flooding displaced the usual hail and wind as the dominant Prairie peril, with record
June and July rainfall in Edmonton. Insurance Bureau of Canada context: insured extreme-weather losses are
up roughly 320% since the late 1990s, with 2024 a record CAD 9.4 billion. A peril-mix shift of this kind is a direct
challenge to the hazard weights in Canadian property models.

report_fields.summary:
Swiss Re Institute models a Cat 5 into Miami or Tampa Bay at over USD 300 billion of market loss, a repeat of
the 1926 Great Miami hurricane at more than USD 200 billion, and a repeat of Hurricane Andrew at close to USD
100 billion. The USD 200 billion spread between the Andrew repeat and a modern Miami/Tampa Cat 5 is driven
almost entirely by landfall location. Against an estimated USD 148 billion of global insured cat losses in a normal
2026, an extreme Florida event would take the annual total past USD 450 billion. Directly usable for tail-scenario
and capital-adequacy stress testing.

occurrences.anchor_text: G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial Chair's Statement

report_fields.summary:
Output of the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial held in Houston 14–16 September, structured around
affordability, supply expansion, diversification, infrastructure and resilience, and innovation. Climate language is
close to absent: the only emissions reference is a neutral list item naming “conventional sources and zero and
low emissions technologies”, with no mention of climate change, decarbonisation targets or climate finance.
Included deliberately, because for transition-risk purposes the absence is the signal — a G20 energy
communiqué stripped of emissions language, combined with the abolition of the Sustainable Finance Working
Group, lowers the probability weight on rapid-transition scenarios and raises it on delayed-and-disorderly and
hot-house pathways. That is a direct input to scenario selection in climate stress testing.

occurrences.anchor_text: wri.org — CDR policy divergence

report_fields.summary:
US federal CDR support has been withdrawn — the DOE Purchase Pilot Prize delayed and direct air capture
hubs halted — while the EU, Canada, Germany and the UK advance beyond voluntary markets, against a need
to remove 2.7–4.1 Gt CO2 per year by 2035. Policy-divergence risk of this kind is a concrete transition-risk driver
and complicates any single global CDR assumption in scenario work.

report_fields.summary:
An ice-and-rock avalanche on the Tibet border triggered a flash flood on 26 August; 359 deaths were confirmed
by 27 August with around 10,000 households affected, and the Trishuli River rose nine metres in thirty minutes.
A textbook cascading, cross-border cryosphere hazard that sits poorly in conventional flood catastrophe models,
and material for Himalayan hydropower and infrastructure exposures.

stated as the first such unequivocal call in its fifty-year history — peaking at very strong intensity around end-
2026 with impacts running into 2027. An unusually high-confidence, multi-quarter shift in the global hazard
baseline for flood, drought, heat and tropical cyclone exposure, spanning two treaty years.

report_fields.summary:
August 2026 was 1.65  °C above the pre-industrial baseline and tied July 2023 as the warmest month ever
recorded, with the highest-ever daily global sea-surface temperature of 21.11 °C, 19 tropical storms and above-
average global cyclone activity. Confirms the physical-risk baseline is running at the top of recent ranges just as
El Niño strengthens — relevant to reserving for the 2026/27 cyclone and heat seasons.
report_fields.title: Earth has hottest August on record

occurrences.anchor_text: Statement: UNEP Report Warns World is Soon to Exceed 1.5 °C — but Return is Possible

report_fields.summary:
WRI responds to the UNEP overshoot finding, arguing return below 1.5 °C remains technically feasible via clean
energy, carbon removal at scale and adaptation, and citing evidence that every US$1 invested in adaptation
yields more than US$10 in benefits. The 10:1 adaptation benefit-cost ratio is a headline figure for protection-gap
and resilience-investment arguments.

verified_information.summary: WASHINGTON (September 2, 2026) — UNEP today published Limiting Overshoot, its first report on the likelihood and consequences of exceeding 1.5°C of global warming. It finds that global temperature rise is set to cross 1.5°C, likely within the next few years, pushing climate risks to increasingly dangerous levels. The report also finds that temperatures can still be brought back down in line with the long-term goals of the Paris Agreement.

occurrences.anchor_text: home.treasury.gov — G20 Chair's Statement, Asheville
occurrences.display_summary: The G20 Chair's statement from the second 2026 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors meeting in Asheville outlines priorities including private sector engagement, productivity, global imbalances, sovereign debt, digital assets and financial sector issues.

report_fields.summary:
The 2026 finance-track priorities are private sector engagement, productivity growth, global imbalances, financial
literacy, sovereign debt, digital assets and financial sector issues. Climate, sustainable finance and energy
transition are absent as policy areas, with energy referenced only as a value chain amid Strait of Hormuz
disruption. This confirms the G20 has ceased to function as a venue for climate-risk and protection-gap work —
removing a channel that as recently as July 2025 convened a side event on the natural catastrophe insurance
protection gap.

report_fields.summary:
Details the 26 August Bhote Koshi–Trishuli flood: over 1,000 deaths, roughly 1,800 hectares of mostly paddy
destroyed, nearly 7,700 tonnes of production lost, 5–10% of livestock and poultry lost across 11 municipalities,
and 41 bridges destroyed. A rare event-level dataset of agricultural and infrastructure loss quantities suitable for
calibrating flood catastrophe and index-insurance parameters, with an explicit second-order missed-planting-
season loss channel.

report_fields.summary:
The underlying quarterly bulletin gives roughly 100% probability of El Niño for both SON 2026 and DJF 2026–27,
driven by persistent and intensifying positive sea-surface temperature anomalies in the central-eastern
equatorial Pacific, and explicitly does not anticipate neutral or La Niña conditions. This is the authoritative input
document behind the press release and the one to cite in catastrophe-model conditioning.
Date note. The publications index and media advisory give a 3 September 2026 release date, while the page byline
shows created 26 August and updated 1 September. The public release date is used here. The bulletin is titled "August
2026" because it is the August-cycle edition.

occurrences.anchor_text: blog.alliedoffsets.com — US carbon market supply and demand
occurrences.display_summary:
The US carbon market is growing on the supply side and narrowing on the demand side
IN WINDOW 11 SEP 2026 ANALYSIS
US issuance (93 Mt) and retirement (34 Mt) lead globally, but domestic buyers took 77% of US credit volume in
2026, up from 63% in 2024, with Microsoft alone accounting for 31% of US retirements; exclusion from Article 6
and CORSIA authorisation after the Paris withdrawal is estimated to cost US$1.5–2.7bn a year in forgone
revenue. Extreme single-buyer concentration is a counterparty and price-stability risk for anyone valuing carbon-
credit assets or offset-dependent transition plans.
📎  Source: blog.alliedoffsets.com — US carbon market supply and demand

occurrences.anchor_text: fao.org — Food Price Index, August 2026
occurrences.display_summary:
Supply concerns drive FAO Food Price Index higher in August
IN WINDOW 4 SEP 2026 PRESS RELEASE
The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9% from July and 2.5% year-on-year.
FAO linked supply concerns to high temperatures and other weather risks, alongside geopolitical and trade disruptions.
Hot, dry weather weakened European wheat prospects and milk supply. El Niño-related conditions affected palm-oil
supply expectations and the global rice forecast. FAO's lower global maize forecast reflects worsening prospects
in France and Poland. These observations connect physical climate risks with measured food commodity prices.
📎 Source: fao.org — Food Price Index, August 2026

report_fields.summary:
The index reached 133.3 points in August, up 1.9% month-on-month and 2.5% year-on-year, with FAO explicitly
attributing gains to high temperatures and drought in France, Poland and the wider EU cutting wheat prospects,
El Niño conditions hitting palm oil and Asian rice, and hot dry weather tightening European milk supply. A clean,
citable link from physical hazard to a monthly quantified commodity price series, usable in inflation and
agricultural insurance modelling.

occurrences.anchor_text: How Might a 'Super El Niño' Affect Food, Forests and Water?

report_fields.summary:
NOAA puts the probability of a very strong El Niño during Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter 2026–27 at
over 90%, with drought risk concentrated in the Caribbean, Central America, northern Brazil and Southeast Asia,
marine heatwave risk to fisheries, and record Amazon fire activity projected for late 2027. Highly actionable near-
term catastrophe-risk intelligence for agricultural, property and marine exposures. The page is dated 28 August
as an update to a 3 June original.
report_fields.title: How Might a 'Super El Niño' Affect Food, Forests and Water?

occurrences.summary:
How Might a 'Super El Niño' Affect Food, Forests and Water?
IN WINDOW 28 AUG 2026 ANALYSIS
NOAA puts the probability of a very strong El Niño during Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter 2026–27 at
over 90%, with drought risk concentrated in the Caribbean, Central America, northern Brazil and Southeast Asia,
marine heatwave risk to fisheries, and record Amazon fire activity projected for late 2027. Highly actionable near-
term catastrophe-risk intelligence for agricultural, property and marine exposures. The page is dated 28 August
as an update to a 3 June original.
📎  Source: wri.org — Super El Niño impacts

verified_information.summary: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), or El Niño, weather pattern occurs naturally every two to seven years, making some parts of the world drier and others wetter. But this year’s El Niño is shaping up to be a different beast. In August 2026, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) reported that El Niño had returned and was getting stronger, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter of 2026-2027.

occurrences.anchor_text: ilo.org — El Niño 2026–2027 and the world of work
occurrences.summary:
El Niño 2026–2027 and the world of work in Latin America and the Caribbean: a causal chain from climate
to employment and labour institutions
1–10 AUG 3 AUG 2026 POLICY BRIEF
Traces how the current El Niño transmits through rainfall and ecosystem change into food security, public health, disaster
risk and then employment and incomes, flagging informal, rural and outdoor workers and identifying vulnerable
subregions and sectors. Useful as a transmission-channel framework for forward-looking scenario work, though it
contains no numeric projections.
📎  Source: ilo.org — El Niño 2026–2027 and the world of work

verified_information.summary: This policy brief examines the potential effects of El Niño 2026–2027 on employment, incomes and working conditions in Latin America and the Caribbean. It identifies the sectors, territories and groups of workers most exposed to droughts, extreme rainfall, flooding and heatwaves, and considers related risks to food security, occupational safety and health, and child labour. The brief emphasizes that these impacts are not predetermined and outlines short-, medium- and long-term policy responses to mitigate labour market impacts and protect exposed workers and communities.

report_fields.source_label: carbonaccountingfinancials.com — PwC joins Accredited Partner Program
report_fields.summary:
PwC becomes a PCAF Global Accredited Partner, offering emissions baselining, calculation automation, data
governance, target-setting and assurance readiness to financial institutions, framed against IFRS S2 and CSRD
requirements. The assurance angle is the significant part: financed-emissions figures are moving from voluntary
disclosure toward audited numbers, raising the evidential standard for the emissions data feeding transition-risk models.

occurrences.anchor_text: El Niño impacts Greater Horn of Africa

report_fields.source_label: wmo.int — El Niño impacts Greater Horn of Africa
report_fields.summary:
ICPAC's Kigali outlook of 17–18 August forecasts a warmer and wetter final quarter of 2026 for the Greater Horn, where
October–December supplies up to 70% of annual rainfall in parts of Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia, with 1997 and 2023 as
stated analogues. Sharply raises flood, crop-damage, infrastructure and disease-outbreak risk in a region with thin
insurance penetration — a live signal for parametric products and sovereign disaster-risk pools.

exposure.

occurrences.anchor_text: wri.org — Rescinding the SEC climate disclosure rule
occurrences.summary:
Rescinding US SEC's Disclosure Rule Will Blindfold Investors to Climate Risk
UPDATED 4 AUG PUBLISHED 31 JUL 2026 COMMENTARY
Argues against rescission of the SEC's 2024 climate disclosure rule, citing 320 institutional investors managing US$50tn
backing standardised disclosure, an average of 20 separate billion-dollar US weather disasters annually, and US$2.3tn of
global energy-transition investment in 2025. Arguably the most consequential item this cycle for practitioners: loss of
mandatory US physical- and transition-risk disclosure degrades the input data available for portfolio climate risk
assessment and pension-fund scenario work.
📎  Source: wri.org — Rescinding the SEC climate disclosure rule

occurrences.anchor_text: ilo.org — heat and worker mortality in Colombia

report_fields.source_label: ilo.org — heat and worker mortality in Colombia
report_fields.summary:
Above 32 °C, excess mortality reaches 0.09 deaths per 1,000 workers overall, rising to 1.33 for assemblers, 0.40 for
health associate professionals, 0.26 for agricultural workers and 0.21 for teaching professionals; between 26 and 32 °C
the excess is 0.04 per 1,000. These are directly applicable occupational heat-mortality loadings for life, disability and
workers' compensation pricing, and the finding that only 53% of Colombia's workforce held occupational-risk cover in
December 2024 quantifies the associated protection gap.

occurrences.anchor_text: climatepromise.undp.org — Chile climate finance

report_fields.summary:
Chile has institutionalised climate expenditure tagging through its Budget Law and Framework Law on Climate Change,
with adaptation's share of tagged spend falling from 81.9% in 2022 as mitigation rose to 30.8% by 2024; it estimates
US$62.3bn of investment is needed, 78–86% of it private. Relevant to assessing transition-finance gaps and the
credibility of sovereign climate investment plans.

occurrences.anchor_text: El Niño's hidden losses: when one season's damage fuels the next crisis
occurrences.summary:
El Niño's hidden losses: when one season's damage fuels the next crisis
OUTSIDE WINDOW 20 JUL 2026 ANALYSIS
Examines how El Niño damage compounds across seasons through failed crops, dead livestock, flooded fields and lost
income — the multi-year loss persistence that single-season catastrophe models tend to understate. Included because
FAO published no in-window climate item and this remains its most recent climate-focused output.
📎  Source: fao.org — El Niño's hidden losses

verified_information.summary: Climate Change El Niño’s hidden losses: when one season’s damage fuels the next crisis 20/07/2026 When El Niño-linked weather extremes hit agrifood systems, the damage can be counted in failed crops, dead livestock, flooded fields and lost income. But the real cost often begins where that first tally ends. One failed season can degrade soils, deplete seed stocks, reduce herds and deepen debt, leaving families less able to recover before the next climate crisis hits.

occurrences.anchor_text: How Egypt is strengthening coastal adaptation in the Nile Delta

report_fields.summary:
A US$105.2m programme — a US$31.4m Green Climate Fund grant plus US$73.8m of government co-financing — has
delivered 69 of a planned 75 km of eco-engineered sea defences, seven sea-level monitoring stations and an integrated
coastal zone management plan covering roughly 1,200 km of coast, protecting 768,000 direct and 17 million indirect
beneficiaries. A rare worked example of adaptation cost per person protected, usable in coastal-flood loss-avoidance and
adaptation-benefit modelling.

IN WINDOW 19 AUG 2026 CASE STUDY
A US$105.2m programme — a US$31.4m Green Climate Fund grant plus US$73.8m of government co-financing — has
delivered 69 of a planned 75 km of eco-engineered sea defences, seven sea-level monitoring stations and an integrated
coastal zone management plan covering roughly 1,200 km of coast, protecting 768,000 direct and 17 million indirect
beneficiaries. A rare worked example of adaptation cost per person protected, usable in coastal-flood loss-avoidance and

verified_information.summary: Stretching across the northern edge of the country, the Nile Delta is one of Egypt’s most productive and densely populated regions. Home to millions of people, it supports critical infrastructure, thriving coastal communities and some of the country’s most valuable agricultural land. Yet it is also among the areas most vulnerable to climate change.

report_fields.summary:

coastal zone management plan covering roughly 1,200 km of coast, protecting 768,000 direct and 17 million indirect
beneficiaries. A rare worked example of adaptation cost per person protected, usable in coastal-flood loss-avoidance and
adaptation-benefit modelling.

and material for Himalayan hydropower and infrastructure exposures.

occurrences.display_summary:
Supply concerns drive FAO Food Price Index higher in August
IN WINDOW 4 SEP 2026 PRESS RELEASE
The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9% from July and 2.5% year-on-year.
FAO linked supply concerns to high temperatures and other weather risks, alongside geopolitical and trade disruptions.
Hot, dry weather weakened European wheat prospects and milk supply. El Niño-related conditions affected palm-oil
supply expectations and the global rice forecast. FAO's lower global maize forecast reflects worsening prospects
in France and Poland. These observations connect physical climate risks with measured food commodity prices.
📎 Source: fao.org — Food Price Index, August 2026

IN WINDOW 11 SEP 2026 ANALYSIS
US issuance (93 Mt) and retirement (34 Mt) lead globally, but domestic buyers took 77% of US credit volume in
2026, up from 63% in 2024, with Microsoft alone accounting for 31% of US retirements; exclusion from Article 6
and CORSIA authorisation after the Paris withdrawal is estimated to cost US$1.5–2.7bn a year in forgone
revenue. Extreme single-buyer concentration is a counterparty and price-stability risk for anyone valuing carbon-
credit assets or offset-dependent transition plans.

report_fields.source_label: ilo.org — heat and worker mortality in Colombia
report_fields.summary:
Above 32 °C, excess mortality reaches 0.09 deaths per 1,000 workers overall, rising to 1.33 for assemblers, 0.40 for
health associate professionals, 0.26 for agricultural workers and 0.21 for teaching professionals; between 26 and 32 °C
the excess is 0.04 per 1,000. These are directly applicable occupational heat-mortality loadings for life, disability and
workers' compensation pricing, and the finding that only 53% of Colombia's workforce held occupational-risk cover in
December 2024 quantifies the associated protection gap.

verified_information.summary: Climate Change El Niño’s hidden losses: when one season’s damage fuels the next crisis 20/07/2026 When El Niño-linked weather extremes hit agrifood systems, the damage can be counted in failed crops, dead livestock, flooded fields and lost income. But the real cost often begins where that first tally ends. One failed season can degrade soils, deplete seed stocks, reduce herds and deepen debt, leaving families less able to recover before the next climate crisis hits.

occurrences.summary:
El Niño 2026–2027 and the world of work in Latin America and the Caribbean: a causal chain from climate
to employment and labour institutions
1–10 AUG 3 AUG 2026 POLICY BRIEF
Traces how the current El Niño transmits through rainfall and ecosystem change into food security, public health, disaster
risk and then employment and incomes, flagging informal, rural and outdoor workers and identifying vulnerable
subregions and sectors. Useful as a transmission-channel framework for forward-looking scenario work, though it
contains no numeric projections.

verified_information.summary: This policy brief examines the potential effects of El Niño 2026–2027 on employment, incomes and working conditions in Latin America and the Caribbean. It identifies the sectors, territories and groups of workers most exposed to droughts, extreme rainfall, flooding and heatwaves, and considers related risks to food security, occupational safety and health, and child labour. The brief emphasizes that these impacts are not predetermined and outlines short-, medium- and long-term policy responses to mitigate labour market impacts and protect exposed workers and communities.

occurrences.anchor_text: US Department of Energy, 16 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Output of the G20 Energy Abundance Ministerial held in Houston 14–16 September, structured around
affordability, supply expansion, diversification, infrastructure and resilience, and innovation. Climate language is
close to absent: the only emissions reference is a neutral list item naming “conventional sources and zero and
low emissions technologies”, with no mention of climate change, decarbonisation targets or climate finance.
Included deliberately, because for transition-risk purposes the absence is the signal — a G20 energy
communiqué stripped of emissions language, combined with the abolition of the Sustainable Finance Working
Group, lowers the probability weight on rapid-transition scenarios and raises it on delayed-and-disorderly and
hot-house pathways. That is a direct input to scenario selection in climate stress testing.

occurrences.anchor_text: Cat 5 Florida hurricanes could drive $300bn plus insurance market loss: Swiss Re

report_fields.summary:
Swiss Re Institute models a Cat 5 into Miami or Tampa Bay at over USD 300 billion of market loss, a repeat of
the 1926 Great Miami hurricane at more than USD 200 billion, and a repeat of Hurricane Andrew at close to USD
100 billion. The USD 200 billion spread between the Andrew repeat and a modern Miami/Tampa Cat 5 is driven
almost entirely by landfall location. Against an estimated USD 148 billion of global insured cat losses in a normal
2026, an extreme Florida event would take the annual total past USD 450 billion. Directly usable for tail-scenario
and capital-adequacy stress testing.

occurrences.anchor_text: Summer storms across the Canadian Prairies caused over $1.8bn in insured losses: CatIQ

report_fields.summary:
CatIQ tallies over CAD 1.8 billion of insured losses from ten extreme weather events across Alberta,
Saskatchewan and Manitoba in summer 2026, the 9–10 June Saskatchewan/Manitoba severe storms alone at
CAD 900 million. Notably, flooding displaced the usual hail and wind as the dominant Prairie peril, with record
June and July rainfall in Edmonton. Insurance Bureau of Canada context: insured extreme-weather losses are
up roughly 320% since the late 1990s, with 2024 a record CAD 9.4 billion. A peril-mix shift of this kind is a direct
challenge to the hazard weights in Canadian property models.

verified_primary_display.title: Cool Leaders, a roadmap and nature for cooling: Global Cooling Pledge acts on heat

occurrences.anchor_text: Cool Leaders, a roadmap and nature for cooling: Global Cooling Pledge acts on heat

report_fields.summary:
At the Global Cooling Pledge Assembly in Singapore UNEP launched a Global Roadmap on Heat Resilience
covering schools, hospitals and energy systems, a Manufacturing Platform for efficient low-GWP equipment, and
the inaugural Cool Leaders awards; Brazil, Cambodia and Côte d'Ivoire launched a Nature for Cooling Challenge
backed by a USD 3 million GEF grant plus USD 33 million co-financing, targeting nature-based cooling that can
cut peak summer temperatures by up to 5°C. Global air-conditioner demand is projected to reach 5.6 billion units
by 2050, nearly triple today's level. Direct read-across to heat mortality and morbidity assumptions in life and
health portfolios, to heat-driven business interruption, and to the electricity-demand and HFC transition
exposures in the cooling value chain.

report_fields.summary:
Marsh Re reports a 50% increase in traded limits for property aggregate excess-of-loss, with nearly 40% of
buyers now building frequency protection into excess-of-loss strategies, up from just over 25% two years ago;
property retro quota share limits placed exceed USD 20 billion, up 30% over four years. The return of aggregate
and frequency cover is the market's direct response to secondary-peril loss frequency — the structural feature
that had been priced out after 2022 — and it changes the shape of the protection available for climate-driven
attritional loss.

has served more than 9 million users from 170-plus countries since 2014 — into Global Nature Watch, extending
near-real-time alerting beyond forests to grasslands and other vegetated ecosystems, with greenhouse gas
dynamics to follow, and a preview AI and geospatial interface called Horizon. Free, near-real-time ecosystem-
change data that can underpin TNFD LEAP location assessments and nature-related exposure screening at
portfolio level.

occurrences.anchor_text: Artemis, 22–23 September 2026 (updated)

report_fields.summary:
Hurricane Polo's intensification put the USD 175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric cat bond in
focus. The bond triggers on central pressure and location, requiring central pressure at or below 937 mb, with
payouts of 25% to 100% of principal by intensity and landfall location. Polo reached Category 5 with central
pressure as low as 892 mb while offshore, then weakened to 120 mph and 954 mb approaching Baja landfall,
making a trigger unlikely. A textbook illustration of parametric basis risk: peak intensity far inside the trigger
threshold, but in the wrong place at the wrong time.

report_fields.summary:
The Hindu Kush Himalaya supplies water to over 240 million people in the region and nearly two billion
downstream across 16 countries. Glacial ice was lost 65% faster in the 2010s than in the previous decade, with
projected 80% volume loss by 2100 on current emissions; the 2022 South Asian heatwave affected over one
billion people and the 2022 Pakistan floods hit 33 million people with over USD 30 billion in damage. Relevant to
compound physical-risk and correlated-loss assessment — glacial lake outburst flood, riverine flood and heat —
across a transboundary exposure base with very thin insurance penetration.

occurrences.anchor_text: Artemis, 25 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
AM Best reports cat bond loss multiples compressing to 2.5x in H1 2026 from 3.28x in H1 2025, with 2026 year-
to-date at 2.4x against 3.0x in 2025 and 3.71x in 2024. Weighted average spread fell 96 basis points while
expected loss on new issuance rose 30 basis points against H1 2025 — investors are being paid less for more
risk. Returns at 30 June 2026: Swiss Re Global Cat Bond Index 4.1%, ILS Advisers Index 3.9%. The
simultaneous fall in multiple and rise in expected loss is the sharpest risk-adjusted-return warning of the window
and bears directly on the cost and reliability of alternative capacity into the January 2027 renewals.

occurrences.anchor_text: Artemis, 17 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
Allstate reported USD 748 million of pre-tax catastrophe losses in August 2026 from 21 separate events, half
from a single wind and hail occurrence, taking April–August aggregate pre-tax cat losses to USD 3.15 billion. Its
only current annual aggregate protection is the USD 150 million Class B tranche of Sanders Re III (Series 2023-
1), attaching at USD 4.78 billion with a USD 50 million per-event deductible, while a new USD 1 billion aggregate
excess-of-loss layer for 2026 attaches at USD 8.5 billion with a USD 1 million event deductible. A clean worked
illustration of how per-event deductibles inside aggregate structures create qualifying-loss uncertainty — a live
reserving and disclosure problem.

costed combined adaptation needs of USD 566 billion across national plans — about USD 56 billion a year — of
which at least USD 80 billion is specifically agricultural, and that is a floor because 22 countries have not
itemised agriculture separately. This is the most usable denominator published this fortnight for African
adaptation protection-gap and sovereign-risk work.

occurrences.anchor_text: NZAOA calls on private market asset managers to turn climate ambition into everyday practice

report_fields.summary:
The 85-member Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance published an updated Call to Action to Private Market Asset
Managers setting seven expectations of general partners across private equity, private debt, infrastructure and
real estate, including firm-level net-zero alignment, better financed-emissions data quality, engagement-led
decarbonisation and explicit integration of physical climate risk analysis, anchored on a principle of acting on
data available today rather than waiting for perfect data. Material for life and pension actuaries: private markets
are the segment where climate data is weakest and valuations least mark-to-market, and asset owners are now
setting explicit physical-risk expectations on general partners.

in normal condition were a minority at 34–38% against a 1991–2020 norm of 46%. Glaciers lost mass for a
fourth straight year across all regions, 1,400 gigatonnes over 2023–2025, and nearly two-thirds of monitored
groundwater wells sat outside historical norms. Asia and Africa accounted for at least 50% of water-related
extreme events and over 80% of associated deaths in the last five years. The headline finding — that the cycle
now oscillates between too little and too much rather than trending in one direction — directly degrades
stationarity assumptions in flood and drought models.

report_fields.summary:
The annual ozone bulletin reports the 2025 Antarctic ozone hole as the fourth-to-fifth smallest since severe
depletion was first observed in 1992, with full recovery expected within several decades, and records UV
radiation rising by as much as 20% in parts of Europe since the mid-1990s, driven mainly by reduced cloud
cover. Marginal but retained on two counts: the Kigali Amendment HFC phase-down is a live transition-risk
exposure for the cooling and refrigeration value chain, and the UV trend is a slow-burn morbidity signal for life
and health portfolios.

report_fields.summary:
Swiss Re puts structural trend growth in insured nat-cat losses at 5–7% a year, with European wildfire losses
compounding an estimated 8–11% annually over recent decades. Modelled insured losses could reach roughly
USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak-loss scenario, and a 2017-style hurricane cluster alone pushes annual insured
losses above USD 120 billion, against 2025 global insured nat-cat losses of USD 120 billion. The 5–7% trend
rate is the single most citable figure this fortnight for calibrating loss-trend assumptions in catastrophe pricing
and ORSA scenarios.

occurrences.anchor_text: Climate-resilient T&D networks in Africa

report_fields.summary:
Technical brief framing climate risk assessment for electricity transmission and distribution networks and
integrating resilience measures across the project cycle, covering extreme heat, flooding, wildfire, landslide, and
sand and dust storms against network reliability, asset life and financial viability, with evidence from the
Mauritania–Mali Interconnection, Eastern Ethiopia Grid Reinforcement and Mozambique's Songo-Matambo. The
claimed cost–benefit evidence for adaptation spend is precisely the evidence base most often missing when
pricing resilience investment.
Caveat. Headline figures sit in the downloadable PDF; the landing page carries abstract-level text only.

report_fields.summary:
Fitch finds 60% expect property catastrophe pricing to decline in 2027, a fifth of those by more than 10%, and
86% expect terms and conditions to loosen (58% selectively, 28% broadly). Fewer than 10% rank property or
property cat as a capital-allocation priority. Fitch's read is that persistent excess P&C capital will push
competition into terms-and-conditions erosion rather than headline rate — the more dangerous form of softening,
because loosened attachment points and hours clauses are not visible in rate indices.

occurrences.anchor_text: What is the AO500? AlliedOffsets' carbon price index, explained

report_fields.summary:
Methodology note on the AO500, a retirement-weighted average price across the 500 highest-retirement-volume
carbon projects, built from over 17,000 price inputs a year and refreshed three times weekly; it closed at USD
6.30/t on 18 September 2026 against a 2026 range of USD 3.16–7.07 and a 2026 average to date of USD 6.04
(2024: USD 3.79). The companion Tradable20 index has averaged USD 2.58 below the AO500 in 2026. For
actuaries the AO500/Tradable20 spread is a direct, published measure of liquidity-tier basis risk in carbon-credit
valuation.

occurrences.anchor_text: New FAO report surveys how different livestock production systems can contribute to social, economic and environmental sustainability

report_fields.summary:
Third in an FAO series on the livestock sector's contribution to food security and sustainable agrifood systems.
Livestock supplies a third of global protein and roughly 40% of agricultural GDP (about USD 1.8 trillion) while
contributing 12% of anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, cattle the largest share and enteric methane a
major source; emission profiles differ by system, with low-external-input systems emitting less per unit area and
high-input systems less per kilogram of output. Relevant to transition risk in agricultural lending and insurance
books, and a counterweight to blanket sectoral exclusion approaches.

occurrences.anchor_text: CCRIF lifts parametric risk pool coverage another 14.5% to $1.8bn for current policy year

report_fields.summary:
CCRIF SPC's parametric risk pool has grown to USD 1.8 billion of coverage limits for the current policy year, up
14.5% on June 2026 and 25% on the prior year. Membership stands at 39, with four new members this season
— Jamaica Public Service Company, National Water Commission Jamaica, Nevis Electricity Company and
Nevis Water Department — all utilities, evidencing extension beyond sovereigns into water and electric utilities.
Since 2007 CCRIF has made 82 payouts totalling USD 483 million, disbursed within 14 days of a qualifying
event. The clearest sovereign-risk-pool datapoint of the window and a working example of parametric basis-risk
design at scale.

occurrences.anchor_text: Who buys US carbon credits, and what are they actually buying?

report_fields.summary:
Documents a structural mismatch between policy incentive and buyer behaviour in the US voluntary market:
despite Section 45Q paying USD 180/t for direct air capture, DAC is only 2% of the largest US buyer's portfolio,
while biomass carbon removal and storage accounted for 96% of durable CDR purchase volume in 2025
(BECCS alone 69%). California's compliance programme has issued over 267 million offset credits through
2024, 81% from forest projects. The US CDR buyer base has doubled since 2022 to 69 buyers but average
purchase size has fallen — a thinning, not deepening, market.

report_fields.summary:
The Bermuda Monetary Authority published a stakeholder letter responding to feedback on its January 2026
consultation for a dedicated Parametric Special Purpose Insurer class supporting structured, fully collateralised
parametric risk transfer. The BMA will look to the substance of risk transfer rather than contractual form,
admitting contracts structured as reinsurance, derivatives or swaps provided statutory requirements are met;
existing SPIs may transition, and some may write both indemnity and parametric business case by case. An
amendment to the Insurance Act 1978 is being drafted for Q4 2026. The most consequential regulatory
development of the window for parametric and index-based climate covers.

occurrences.anchor_text: Building Colombia's Nature Economy Could Create Hundreds of Thousands of New Jobs

report_fields.summary:
Estimates 775,000 jobs from nature tourism and agribusiness in Colombia by 2035 against a government-
identified pipeline of more than USD 32 billion in green investment opportunities. The transition-risk figure of note
is that about 4.7 million workers, roughly 22.6% of the current workforce, will be directly affected by the climate
transition, in a labour market where around 55% of workers were informally employed as of June 2026. A
concrete just-transition exposure quantification for an emerging-market sovereign, relevant both to sovereign
transition-risk scenarios and to life and health portfolios exposed to informal-sector displacement.

occurrences.anchor_text: WRI news, 23 September 2026

report_fields.summary:
WRI's response to the UNSG Climate Summit, organised around keeping 1.5°C within reach, mobilising finance
for developing countries, and — new emphasis — advancing adaptation during climate overshoot. Germany
announced a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap to 2045; WRI cites a benefit-cost ratio of more than 10:1
over a decade for adaptation spending. The formal arrival of “adaptation under overshoot” in the multilateral
agenda is the signal for scenario designers: it legitimises planning around temporary exceedance of 1.5°C rather
than treating it as a tail case.

IN WINDOW 23 SEP 2026 PRESS RELEASE ADAPTATION
WRI's response to the UNSG Climate Summit, organised around keeping 1.5°C within reach, mobilising finance
for developing countries, and — new emphasis — advancing adaptation during climate overshoot. Germany
announced a national fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap to 2045; WRI cites a benefit-cost ratio of more than 10:1
over a decade for adaptation spending. The formal arrival of “adaptation under overshoot” in the multilateral
agenda is the signal for scenario designers: it legitimises planning around temporary exceedance of 1.5°C rather
than treating it as a tail case.
📎  Source: WRI news, 23 September 2026

occurrences.anchor_text: ILS can play a broader role in narrowing the global protection gap: Moody's

report_fields.summary:
Moody's argues P&C insurers and reinsurers cannot close the protection gap alone given capital and regulatory
constraints, and positions insurance-linked securities as the marginal capacity source. Alternative capital
reached a record USD 147 billion in H1 2026; H1 2026 cat bond issuance set a record of nearly USD 18 billion;
outstanding cat bond market size was USD 65.6 billion at end-Q2 2026. Moody's cites Hurricane Melissa
(October 2025), which caused an estimated USD 12.2 billion of damage in Jamaica — 54% of GDP — and
triggered a full payout on a World Bank-backed USD 150 million parametric cat bond.

occurrences.anchor_text: iClimateAction publishes three new reports on the climate observation data chain

report_fields.summary:
Three deliverables assessing the observational base underpinning climate services. In-situ networks supporting
the 55 Essential Climate Variables still depend heavily on short-term research projects, in-kind contributions or
volunteers, with material gaps across Africa, South America, Southeast Asia and the polar regions; satellite
observation covers 42 of the 55 ECVs, and a February 2026 survey of 33 climate experts found communication
with decision-makers, not data access or quality, the most-cited barrier to uptake. This is the observational-input
risk sitting underneath every catastrophe model and physical-risk scorecard — known geographic gaps and
funding fragility in the underlying networks are a source of parameter uncertainty that is rarely priced.

occurrences.anchor_text: UNEP FI / TNFD, September 2026

report_fields.summary:
A TNFD guide produced with UNEP FI, structured around ten questions for bank chief risk officers and risk
committees to test exposure to nature-related financial risk across credit and investment portfolios, with the
headline quantification that pollinator decline alone puts up to USD 577 billion of annual global crop production at
risk. It positions nature loss as a systemic financial-stability issue to be handled inside mainstream risk
frameworks rather than as a disclosure exercise, and is the bank-CRO companion to TNFD's earlier CFO and
asset-owner editions. Relevant to actuaries working on nature-related financial risk and on agricultural credit and
crop exposures.
Caveat. Partial verification. The UNEP FI landing page carries “September 2026” only and there is no matching item in
the UNEP FI news listing. Third-party coverage (Sustainable Japan, 18 September 2026) corroborates a release around
17–18 September but also states only the month. Title, URL, content and month are confirmed; the day is approximate.

WRI responds to the UNEP overshoot finding, arguing return below 1.5 °C remains technically feasible via clean
energy, carbon removal at scale and adaptation, and citing evidence that every US$1 invested in adaptation
yields more than US$10 in benefits. The 10:1 adaptation benefit-cost ratio is a headline figure for protection-gap
and resilience-investment arguments.

### Verified information

WASHINGTON (September 2, 2026) — UNEP today published Limiting Overshoot, its first report on the likelihood and consequences of exceeding 1.5°C of global warming. It finds that global temperature rise is set to cross 1.5°C, likely within the next few years, pushing climate risks to increasingly dangerous levels. The report also finds that temperatures can still be brought back down in line with the long-term goals of the Paris Agreement.

An ice-and-rock avalanche on the Tibet border triggered a flash flood on 26 August; 359 deaths were confirmed
by 27 August with around 10,000 households affected, and the Trishuli River rose nine metres in thirty minutes.

As the US Carbon Dioxide Removal Market Retreats, Other Governments Step Up
IN WINDOW 10 SEP 2026 ANALYSIS
US federal CDR support has been withdrawn — the DOE Purchase Pilot Prize delayed and direct air capture
hubs halted — while the EU, Canada, Germany and the UK advance beyond voluntary markets, against a need
to remove 2.7–4.1 Gt CO2 per year by 2035. Policy-divergence risk of this kind is a concrete transition-risk driver
and complicates any single global CDR assumption in scenario work.

IN WINDOW 10 SEP 2026 PRESS RELEASE

# Asking Better Questions on Nature: For Bank Chief Risk Officers and Risk Committees

## PDF report observation: pdf-article-occurrence-ed905dc59281d9e9fa7d91a1

Asking Better Questions on Nature: For Bank Chief Risk Officers and Risk Committees
IN WINDOW SEPTEMBER 2026 GUIDANCE NATURE RISK
A TNFD guide produced with UNEP FI, structured around ten questions for bank chief risk officers and risk
committees to test exposure to nature-related financial risk across credit and investment portfolios, with the
headline quantification that pollinator decline alone puts up to USD 577 billion of annual global crop production at
risk. It positions nature loss as a systemic financial-stability issue to be handled inside mainstream risk
frameworks rather than as a disclosure exercise, and is the bank-CRO companion to TNFD's earlier CFO and
asset-owner editions. Relevant to actuaries working on nature-related financial risk and on agricultural credit and
crop exposures.
Caveat. Partial verification. The UNEP FI landing page carries “September 2026” only and there is no matching item in
the UNEP FI news listing. Third-party coverage (Sustainable Japan, 18 September 2026) corroborates a release around
17–18 September but also states only the month. Title, URL, content and month are confirmed; the day is approximate.

# How Might a 'Super El Niño' Affect Food, Forests and Water?

## PDF report observation: pdf-article-occurrence-f20ad998c549b169baf97ea7

How Might a 'Super El Niño' Affect Food, Forests and Water?
IN WINDOW 28 AUG 2026 ANALYSIS
NOAA puts the probability of a very strong El Niño during Northern Hemisphere autumn and winter 2026–27 at
over 90%, with drought risk concentrated in the Caribbean, Central America, northern Brazil and Southeast Asia,
marine heatwave risk to fisheries, and record Amazon fire activity projected for late 2027. Highly actionable near-
term catastrophe-risk intelligence for agricultural, property and marine exposures. The page is dated 28 August
as an update to a 3 June original.
📎  Source: wri.org — Super El Niño impacts

### Verified information

The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), or El Niño, weather pattern occurs naturally every two to seven years, making some parts of the world drier and others wetter. But this year’s El Niño is shaping up to be a different beast. In August 2026, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) reported that El Niño had returned and was getting stronger, with a greater than 90% chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter of 2026-2027.

# How landlocked countries are prioritizing water in their adaptation planning

How landlocked countries are prioritizing water in their adaptation planning
IN WINDOW 4 SEP 2026 CASE STUDY
National Adaptation Plan progress in Armenia, the Kyrgyz Republic and Uzbekistan under GCF Readiness
funding, citing Armenian groundwater down by two-thirds, the Aral Sea down roughly 90% in volume, and Kyrgyz
reliance on hydropower for about 92% of electricity. Useful exposure detail on cascading water–energy–food
